p.src: Now Chao Gai and the others heard this and asked the strategist, “What flaw is there in this letter?” Wu Yong said, “In my haste this morning, when Director Dai took the reply, I failed to notice something: was the seal I had him use not the four characters ‘Hanlin Cai Jing’ carved in jade-chopstick seal script? That very seal will land Dai Zong in an official prosecution.” Jin Dajian said, “Whenever I have seen Grand Preceptor Cai’s letters and writings, they have all borne this seal. This time I carved it without the slightest error. How could it betray us?” Scholar Wu said, “None of you understands. Prefect Cai the Ninth of Jiangzhou is Grand Preceptor Cai’s son. How could a father writing to his son use a seal bearing the father’s personal name? That is where we went wrong. It was something I failed to foresee. When this man reaches Jiangzhou, he will surely be interrogated and the truth will come out. The consequences will be grave.” Chao Gai said, “Send someone after him at once and call him back. Could we not write another letter?” Scholar Wu said, “How could anyone catch him? Once he invokes his magic traveling art, by now he will already have covered five hundred li. There is no time to lose. We can only act in this way if we are to save both of them.” Chao Gai asked, “How are we to save them? What good plan have you?” Scholar Wu stepped forward and whispered in Chao Gai’s ear, “We shall do this and this, and then thus and thus. Our commander may secretly pass down the order and let everyone know. We must set out exactly as arranged and not miss the appointed time.” Once the many heroes had received their commander’s orders, each packed his gear, descended the mountain that very night, and headed for Jiangzhou. Of this, no more need be said for now. Why does the storyteller not reveal the plan? Rest assured, it will be seen below.

p.src: Meanwhile, Dai Zong kept to the deadline, returned to Jiangzhou, and delivered the reply in the main hall. Prefect Cai the Ninth was delighted to see Dai Zong return on time. He first had three cups of wine brought to reward him, then personally accepted the reply and asked, “Did you see my honored father, the Grand Preceptor?” Dai Zong reported, “This humble servant stayed only one night before returning and had no opportunity to see His Excellency.” The prefect broke the seal and saw that the beginning said all the many articles in the gift hamper had been received; the latter part said that His Present Majesty wished to see the sorcerous rebel Song Jiang himself, and ordered that he be securely confined in a prison cart, closely guarded by reliable officers, and escorted to the capital by night without being allowed to escape along the road; and at the end it said that once Huang Wenbing’s memorial reached the emperor, an appointment would surely follow. After reading it, Prefect Cai the Ninth could hardly contain his joy and ordered that Dai Zong be rewarded with an ingot of twenty-five taels of fine silver; at the same time, he ordered a prison cart to be assembled and discussed whom to send as escort when the journey began. Dai Zong thanked him, returned to his lodging, bought some wine and meat, and went to visit Song Jiang in prison. Of this, no more need be said.

p.src: Meanwhile, Prefect Cai the Ninth pressed the workmen to finish the prison cart. A day or two later, just as it was about to depart, a gatekeeper came to report, “Assistant Prefect Huang of Wuwei Commandery has come especially to pay you a visit.” Prefect Cai invited him into the rear hall, where they met. Huang also presented some gifts, including fresh seasonal wine and fruit. The prefect thanked him, saying, “I am repeatedly indebted to your generosity. How can I deserve it?” Huang Wenbing said, “They are merely trifles from the countryside, hardly worth mentioning.” The prefect said, “Congratulations. Before long, you will surely have cause to celebrate an honorable appointment.” Huang Wenbing asked, “How does Your Excellency know this?” The prefect said, “The messenger returned yesterday. The sorcerous rebel Song Jiang is to be escorted to the capital; and before long, Assistant Prefect, your merits will be reported to His Majesty and you will be promoted to high office. My honored father explained the whole matter in his reply.” Huang Wenbing said, “If that is so, I am deeply grateful for His Excellency’s recommendation. The man who carried the letter must truly be a magic traveler.” The prefect said, “If you do not believe me, you may inspect my father’s letter and see that I speak no falsehood.” Huang Wenbing said, “I feared it would be improper for me to presume to read a private family letter; but if Your Excellency entrusts it to me, I beg leave to look it over.” The prefect said at once, “You, Assistant Prefect, are my intimate friend. What harm could there be in your reading it?” He ordered an attendant to fetch the letter and handed it to Huang Wenbing. Huang Wenbing took the letter and read it through from beginning to end. He rolled it up, examined the wrapper, and noticed how fresh the seal was. Shaking his head, Huang Wenbing said, “This letter is not genuine.” The prefect said, “You are mistaken, Assistant Prefect. This is my honored father’s own handwriting, his authentic script. How could it not be genuine?” Huang Wenbing said, “Permit me to explain, Your Excellency. When private letters arrived in the past, did they ever bear this seal?” The prefect said, “The letters that came before never bore this seal; they were merely written out in his own hand. This time, the seal box must have been close at hand, so he conveniently stamped the wrapper with it.” Huang Wenbing said, “My lord, do not blame me for speaking too much! Someone has used this letter to deceive you. The calligraphic styles of Su, Huang, Mi, and Cai are now widely practiced throughout the realm. Who cannot learn to imitate them? Moreover, this seal was one your honored father used when he served as a Hanlin Academician, and many people have seen it in calligraphic models. Now that he has risen to be Grand Preceptor and Chief Minister, how could he still use his old Hanlin seal? Besides, this is a letter from a father to his son. He certainly ought not to use a seal bearing his personal name. Your honored father, the Grand Preceptor, is a man whose learning encompasses all beneath Heaven and whose wisdom and foresight are profound. How could he carelessly make such a mistake? If Your Excellency doubts my words, question the messenger closely about whom he met at the residence. If his account does not match, then the letter is false. Do not blame me for saying too much. Only because you have favored me so generously have I dared to speak beyond my station.” After hearing him, Prefect Cai the Ninth said, “That is easily settled. This man had never been to the Eastern Capital before. A single interrogation will reveal whether his story is true or false.”

When you went to the capital for me, which gate did you enter by?” Dai Zong said, “By the time I reached the Eastern Capital, it was already late, so I do not know what the gate was called.” The prefect asked again, “Who received you at the gate of my family residence? A short while later, the gatekeeper came out, took charge of the letter hampers, and told me to find an inn for myself. p.src: Dai Zong pleaded, “As I passed by Liangshan Marsh, a band of outlaws rushed out, robbed me, bound me, and carried me up the mountain, intending to cut open my belly and tear out my heart. They searched me, found and read the letter, seized both letter hampers, and then spared my life. Knowing I could not return home, I asked only to die on the mountain, but instead they wrote this letter for me so that I could return and escape punishment. Fearing Your Excellency’s punishment, I concealed it from you.” The prefect said, “That may be partly true, but there are still lies in it. Plainly you conspired with the Liangshan Marsh bandits, plotting together to seize my letter hampers and goods. How dare you tell such a tale? Beat the wretch again!” Dai Zong endured their interrogation and torture but steadfastly refused to confess to having dealings with Liangshan Marsh. Prefect Cai Jiu tortured and questioned Dai Zong once more, but his account remained the same from beginning to end. The prefect said, “There is no need to question him further. Bring a heavy cangue, lock it around his neck, and cast him into prison.” He then withdrew from the hall and thanked Huang Wenbing, saying, “But for your keen judgment, Assistant Prefect, I would nearly have bungled a grave affair.” Huang Wenbing said, “It is plain that this man too is allied with Liangshan Marsh. He has conspired with them, joined their treasonous designs, and become one of their faction. Unless he is eliminated, he will surely bring trouble later.” The prefect said, “Then we shall settle the two men’s confessions, draw up the case documents, escort them to the execution ground, and behead them. Afterward, I shall submit a memorial to the court.” Huang Wenbing said, “Your Excellency’s judgment is most enlightened. By doing so, first, the court will be pleased and will know that Your Excellency has performed this great service; and second, the Liangshan Marsh bandits will be prevented from coming to break them out of prison.” The prefect said, “Your foresight, Assistant Prefect, is truly profound. I shall issue the official documents myself and personally recommend you for advancement.” That day he entertained Huang Wenbing, escorted him out through the prefectural gate, and Huang returned to Wuwei Garrison.

p.src: The next day, Prefect Cai Jiu ascended the hall and summoned the clerk in charge of the case. “Hurry and compile the case documents, attaching the confessions and depositions of Song Jiang and Dai Zong. At the same time, write out the placards stating their offenses and have them escorted to the execution ground tomorrow to be beheaded. Since ancient times, those guilty of treason have been executed without awaiting the regular season. Behead Song Jiang and Dai Zong and avert future trouble.” The clerk assigned to the case was Clerk Huang. He was on very good terms with Dai Zong, yet had no means to save him and could only lament bitterly on his behalf. That day he reported, “Tomorrow is a national day of mourning, and the day after is the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the Zhongyuan Festival. No execution may be carried out on either day. The day after that is likewise an auspicious observance of the state. It cannot be done until five days from now.” For one thing, Heaven’s good fortune thus came to Song Jiang’s aid; for another, the heroes of Liangshan Marsh had not yet arrived.

p.src: After hearing this, Prefect Cai Jiu accepted Clerk Huang’s advice. They waited until early on the sixth day. First, men were sent to the crossroads to sweep and prepare the execution ground. After breakfast, local troops, armed guards, and executioners were mustered—more than five hundred men in all—and stationed before the main prison gate. At the hour of the Snake, the prison official reported to the prefect, who came in person to preside over the executions. Clerk Huang had no choice but to present the placards stating the prisoners’ offenses. In the hall, the prefect wrote the character “behead” on each one, and each was then covered with a strip of reed matting. Although the many constables and jailers of Jiangzhou Prefecture were friendly with Dai Zong and Song Jiang, they had no means of saving them. They could only lament bitterly for the two men. Once all preparations were complete, Song Jiang and Dai Zong were bound inside the main prison. Their hair was brushed with glue and tied into goose-pear-shaped topknots, and a red silk-paper flower was stuck into each man’s hair. They were driven before the altar of the Blue-Faced Holy One, where each was given a bowl of last-meal rice and a cup of farewell wine. After eating and drinking, they took leave of the altar, turned around, and had the execution placards fastened to them. Some sixty or seventy jailers put Song Jiang in front and Dai Zong behind, then shoved and herded them out through the prison gate. Song Jiang and Dai Zong looked at each other, but neither could utter a word. Song Jiang could only stamp his feet. Dai Zong lowered his head and sighed. p.src: Sorrowful clouds drifted slowly, and bitter vapors seethed. Overhead the sun had lost its light, while mournful winds howled on every side. Tasseled spears stood rank on rank; a few beats of the drum scattered the three souls. Clubs bristled thick as a forest; a few clangs of the gong hastened away the seven spirits. The placards naming their crimes were raised on high; people wondered when those departing would ever return. Twin white paper flowers swayed; all said that this time they could scarcely leave alive. The last meal before death—they could hardly swallow it past their throats; The wine of eternal farewell—how could they force it down? Ferocious executioners leaned on steel blades, and hideous jailers bore the instruments of the law. Beneath the black banner, countless demons followed behind; At the crossroads, numberless violent ghosts waited. The presiding official hurried to issue his commands, while the coroners prepared to carry away the corpses.

p.src: The executioners summoned all their murderous attendants, and, crowding Song Jiang and Dai Zong from before and behind, escorted them to the crossroads at the public execution ground. Spears and clubs encircled them on every side. They seated Song Jiang facing south with his back to the north, and Dai Zong facing north with his back to the south, there to await the third quarter of the noon hour, when the presiding official would arrive and order the blades to fall. The crowd looked up and read what was written on the placard of charges: “One prisoner of Jiangzhou Prefecture, Song Jiang: for deliberately composing a seditious poem, recklessly spreading treasonous words, joining with the outlaws of Liangshan Marsh, and conspiring with them in rebellion—sentenced by law to be beheaded. One prisoner, Dai Zong: for secretly carrying private letters for Song Jiang, colluding with the outlaws of Liangshan Marsh, and conspiring with them in rebellion—sentenced by law to be beheaded. Presiding official: Cai, Prefect of Jiangzhou.” The prefect reined in his horse and waited for the appointed time to be reported.

p.src: Presently, on the eastern side of the execution ground, a band of beggars who performed with snakes tried to force their way inside to watch. The soldiers beat and drove at them, but they would not retreat. While they were still wrangling, another band appeared on the western side of the ground—men who displayed spear-and-staff fighting and sold medicines. They too began forcing their way in. The soldiers shouted, “What an ignorant rabble you are! Do you not know what place this is, that you force your way in to watch?” The spear-and-staff men replied, “You are the ignorant bumpkins! We have traveled through prefectures and crossed provinces; where have we not been? Everywhere we go, executions are open to spectators. Even when the Son of Heaven executes someone in the imperial capital, the people are allowed to watch. Yet in this petty place, merely beheading two men has thrown the whole world into an uproar. We will just push inside and take a look. Why make such a damned fuss about it?” As they began quarreling with the soldiers, the presiding official shouted, “Drive them back for now! Do not let them come near!” Before that disturbance had ended, a group of porters carrying shoulder loads appeared at the southern side of the ground and tried to push their way in. The soldiers shouted, “An execution is taking place here! Where are you carrying those loads?” The men replied, “We are delivering these goods to His Excellency the prefect. How dare you obstruct us?” The soldiers said, “Even if you belong to His Excellency’s own office, you must still go around by another way.” The men set down their loads, pulled out their carrying poles, and stood among the crowd to watch. Then a party of traveling merchants appeared at the northern side of the execution ground, pushing two carts toward it and insisting on entering. The soldiers shouted, “Where are you people going?” The travelers answered, “We must press on with our journey. Let us pass.” The soldiers said, “An execution is taking place here. How could we possibly let you through? If you are in haste, take another road.” The travelers laughed. “That is easy for you to say. We have come all the way from the imperial capital and know nothing of the damned roads here. We only know to follow this highway.” The soldiers still refused to let them pass, so the travelers pressed forward together and stood their ground. The clamor continued on every side, and Prefect Cai the Ninth found himself unable to restrain it. He also saw that the travelers had all climbed onto the carts and stood there watching.

p.src: From amid the crowd appeared a huge black fellow, brandishing two broad axes and hacking his way forward without pause. Chao Gai and the others did not know him, but saw that he fought harder and killed more men than anyone else. Chao Gai suddenly remembered that Dai Zong had once spoken of Li Kui, the “Black Whirlwind,” who was Song Sanlang’s closest friend and a recklessly impetuous man. Chao Gai called out, “You valiant fellow up ahead—are you not the ‘Black Whirlwind’?” But the man would not answer. In a blazing fury, he swung his great axes and thought of nothing but cutting people down. Chao Gai ordered the two underlings carrying Song Jiang and Dai Zong to keep close behind the huge black fellow. When they reached the crossroads, they killed soldiers and civilians indiscriminately. Corpses lay everywhere, blood ran in channels, and countless people were knocked down and trampled underfoot. The chiefs abandoned their carts and baggage poles, and the whole company followed the huge black fellow, fighting their way straight out of the city; Behind them, Hua Rong, Huang Xin, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng loosed arrows from four bows, sending them backward like a swarm of locusts. Who among the soldiers and people of Jiangzhou dared come near them? The huge black fellow fought all the way to the riverbank, his body drenched in spattered blood, and even there he continued killing. Chao Gai raised his staff-sabre and shouted, “The common people have nothing to do with this! Stop harming them!” But the man paid no heed to the cry. One stroke, one victim—he hewed them down in a row. After following the river for some five or seven li from the city, they saw ahead only the vast, surging river; the road over land had come to an end. Seeing this, Chao Gai could only cry out in dismay. Only then did the huge black fellow call out, “Don’t panic. Carry our brother into the temple for now.”

p.src: When they all looked, they saw a great temple beside the river, its double doors tightly shut. The huge black fellow smashed them open with two blows of his axes and rushed inside. Chao Gai and the others looked around. Ancient cypresses and venerable pines stood on either side, their foliage casting deep shade. On the tablet ahead, four great characters were written in gold: “Temple of the White Dragon God.” The underlings carried Song Jiang and Dai Zong into the temple and laid them down to rest. Only then did Song Jiang dare open his eyes. Seeing Chao Gai and the others, he wept and said, “Brother, can this be a meeting in a dream?” Chao Gai consoled him, saying, “My dear brother, you refused to stay with us in the stronghold, and so have suffered this misery today. Who is that huge black fellow who fought so fiercely?” Song Jiang replied, “That is Li Kui, the man called the ‘Black Whirlwind.’ Several times he wanted to free me from prison, but I feared we could not escape and would not consent.” Chao Gai said, “What a rare man! He labored hardest of all and feared neither blades, axes, nor arrows.” Hua Rong called out, “First bring clothes for our two elder brothers to put on.” While they were reunited, Li Kui emerged from beneath the corridor, carrying his pair of axes. Song Jiang stopped him and asked, “Brother, where are you going?” Li Kui answered, “To find the temple keeper and kill him too! Curse that wretch—he did not come out to receive us and even shut the damned temple doors against us. I meant to seize him and offer him as a sacrifice to the gate, but I cannot find the wretch.” Song Jiang said, “Come here first and meet my elder brother and the other chiefs.” Hearing this, Li Kui dropped his axes, knelt before Chao Gai, and said, “Elder Brother, please forgive Iron Ox for his boorish ways.” After he had greeted everyone, he recognized Zhu Gui as a man from his own native district, and both were delighted. Hua Rong then said, “Brother, you ordered everyone to follow Brother Li without stopping, and now we have come here only to find the great river blocking our way ahead. This is a dead end, and not a single boat is waiting to aid us. If the government troops pursue us out of the city, how are we to meet them? What aid can we rely upon?” Li Kui said, “Don’t panic! I’ll go back into the city with you, and we’ll cut down that damned Prefect Cai Jiu as well before we leave.” Only now did Dai Zong regain consciousness. He called out, “Brother, you must not give rein to your recklessness. There are five or seven thousand troops in the city. If we fight our way back in, disaster is certain.” Ruan Xiaoqi said, “Across the river in the distance, I can see several boats by the bank. What if we three brothers swim over, seize those boats, and bring them here to carry everyone across?” Chao Gai said, “That is the best plan.”

p.src: From the bow of his boat, Zhang Shun saw them and shouted, “What manner of people are you? Zhang Heng had brought Mu Hong, Mu Chun, and Xue Yong, together with more than ten retainers from the manor, in another boat. In the third boat, Li Jun had brought Li Li, Tong Wei, and Tong Meng, along with more than ten salt-trading boatmen. All came ashore bearing spears and staves. Overjoyed at seeing Song Jiang, Zhang Shun bowed and said, “Ever since you became entangled in this case, Elder Brother, I have been unable to sit or stand at ease, yet could find no way to rescue you. I had no choice but to seek out my own elder brother and bring him to Squire Mu’s manor, where we summoned many of our acquaintances. Today we were on our way to fight into Jiangzhou, break open the prison, and rescue you. We never expected that other valiant men had already saved you and brought you here. May I venture to ask whether these heroes are the righteous men of Liangshan Marsh, led by Heavenly King Chao?” Pointing to the man standing in the place of honor, Song Jiang said, “This is my elder brother Chao Gai. All of you, come into the temple and exchange proper greetings.” Zhang Shun’s nine men, Chao Gai’s seventeen, and Song Jiang, Dai Zong, and Li Kui—twenty-nine men in all—gathered inside the White Dragon Temple. This came to be called “The Small Gathering at the White Dragon Temple.”

u.src: After the twenty-nine heroes had exchanged all due courtesies, an underling suddenly rushed into the temple in alarm and reported, “Gongs and drums are sounding inside Jiangzhou. The troops are mustering and have left the city in pursuit.

From afar we can see banners blotting out the sun and swords thick as hemp. Armored cavalry lead the column, while behind them come ranks of soldiers with spears raised. Brandishing great blades and broad axes, they are charging along the road toward the White Dragon Temple.”

p.src: Hearing this, Li Kui gave a great shout: “Let’s charge in and kill them!” Gripping his twin axes, he strode out through the temple gate. Chao Gai cried, “Once begun, we must see this through! Let all you gallant heroes lend me, Chao Gai, your aid. We shall not return to Liangshan Marsh until we have utterly destroyed the troops of Jiangzhou!” The heroes answered with one voice, “We shall obey your command!” All hundred and forty or fifty men raised a battle cry together and charged toward the Jiangzhou shore. And so blood would dye the waves crimson and corpses would pile up like mountains, while leaping azure dragons spewed venomous fire and mountain-roaming fierce tigers roared into the winds of heaven. How Chao Gai and the other gallant heroes ultimately made their escape will be revealed in the next chapter.
